# sogni-client Rust SDK complete agent reference

Crate version: 5.27.1. Unreleased compatibility includes TypeScript 5.32.0
(upstream commit 18b43c9). Crate path: `sogni_client`.
Async runtime: Tokio. All public network methods return
`sogni_client::Result<T>`.

## Construction and authentication

`SogniClient::builder()` returns `ClientBuilder`.

Builder methods: `app_id`, `app_source`, `attribution`, `network`, `api_key`,
`tokens`, `cookie_auth`, `rest_endpoint`, `socket_endpoint`, `disable_socket`,
`testnet`, `request_timeout`, `connect_timeout`,
`socket_event_subscription`, and async `build`.

Default REST endpoint: `https://api.sogni.ai`.
Default socket endpoint: `wss://socket.sogni.ai`.
Networks: `Network::Fast`, `Network::Relaxed`.

WebSocket clients require an explicit, nonblank `app_id`, trimmed during
construction. Generate it once and persist it across restarts. There is no
random per-start default. `disable_socket(true)` needs no ID, uses `rest-only`
when omitted, and never connects a WebSocket. `defer_socket_start(true)` still
requires a stable app ID because later socket commands can open a connection.

API-key authentication starts automatically. Token authentication accepts the
Authorization value and refresh token; JWT expiry drives refresh through
`/v1/account/refresh-token`. `check_auth` is only for cookie-auth flows.
Username/password authentication requires the default `wallet` feature and is
available through `account.login` or `account.create_account`.

## AccountApi

Methods: `get_nonce`, `login`, `login_with_options`, `create_account`, `logout`,
`me`, `account_balance`, `refresh_balance`, `wallet_balance`,
`validate_username`, `switch_network`, `transaction_history`, `rewards`,
`claim_rewards`, `withdraw`, `deposit`, `approve_token_usage`,
`get_subscription_status`, `get_subscription_usage`, `get_trial_eligibility`,
`set_device_id`, `get_subscription_plans`, `create_subscription_checkout`, and
`create_subscription_portal_session`.

`current_account()` returns a cheap cloneable handle. `snapshot()` is the raw
serializable state. Convenience getters expose username, email, wallet,
balance, subscription, free-Spark lock state, network, and unlimited
entitlement. Versioned socket subscription events remain authoritative over
older in-flight REST refreshes. `subscribe()` emits updates.

## ProjectsApi

Construct requests with `ProjectRequest::image`, `video`, or `audio`. All set
`type`, `modelId`, `positivePrompt`, and default `numberOfMedia=1`. Builder
methods: `param`, `number_of_media`, `steps`, `guidance`, `dimensions`,
`duration`, `fps`, `network`, `asset`, `sam3_prompt`,
`world_generation_receipt`, and `attribution`.

`MediaSource::Path` performs async file I/O. `MediaSource::bytes` and
`named_bytes` accept memory. `AssetRole` includes starting/control/context
images and video/audio/mask roles. `ReferenceAudioSlot(1..=3)` and
`ReferenceVideoSlot(1..=3)` map MiniMax H3 r2v's numbered, contiguous media
slots. Adding any asset enables its matching wire flag. `Custom` carries a
forward-compatible wire name and whether the media endpoint is required.

`projects.create(request)` uploads assets, submits `jobRequest`, and returns a
cloneable `Project`. `Project` methods: `id`, `status`, `jobs`, `progress`,
`result_urls`, `snapshot`, `subscribe`, `wait_for_completion`, `cancel`.
`Job` methods: `snapshot`, `id`, `status`, `progress`, `result_url`,
`is_withheld`, `has_result_media`, `subscribe`, `get_result_url`,
`get_result_data`, `enhance`, `enhancement_project`, `media_type`,
`preparation`, and `provenance`.

SAM3: use `ProjectRequest::image("sam3_image_segment_bf16", "")` with
`AssetRole::StartingImage` and `Sam3ImagePrompt`. It forces numberOfMedia=1,
numberOfPreviews=0, and outputFormat=png in both the request and project state.
Points use x/y in [0,1] and Sam3PointLabel::Positive or Negative. Boxes use
x0/y0/x1/y1 in [0,1], with x0<x1 and y0<y1. At least one point, box, or text
prompt is required. Limits: 32 points, 16 boxes, 240 UTF-16 text code units.
Text and points cannot be combined; points allow at most one box. Optional
threshold defaults to 0.5 and multimask to true. Unknown prompt fields fail.

Pixal3D: `ProjectRequest::image("pixal3d_int8_i23d", prompt)` requires a
starting image. Wire outputFormat is always glb. `job.media_type()` is model;
result URL lookups and recovery use /v1/media/downloadUrl with
contentType=model/gltf-binary. Model artifacts cannot use image enhancement.
`is_model_artifact_model` recognizes pixal3d_ IDs; the ProjectsApi method
`is_model_artifact_model_id` prefers advertised model metadata.

`JobProvenance` includes optional sha256, source_image_sha256,
sam_prompt_sha256, mask_rle_sha256, mask_width, mask_height, sam_version,
selection_hash, first_frame_sha256, and last_frame_sha256. Live and recovered
results normalize valid hashes to lowercase; malformed and unknown fields
are omitted from this projection. `jobCompleted` events include provenance
when present, and JobSnapshot serializes it as camelCase.

`WorldGenerationReceiptRequest::TargetStill` carries source_image_sha256 and
selection_hash for krea2_identity_edit_sogni_v0_3_alpha. `Transition` carries
first_frame_sha256 and last_frame_sha256 for
minimax-h3-fastvideo-int8_flf2v_turbo. Both require appSource=sogni-world;
receipts serialize inside keyFrames[0]. The service verifies uploaded inputs.

`JobPreparation` variants: DownloadingAssets, UnloadingModel, LoadingModel.
Model phases carry model, JobModelPhaseStep::{Start,End}, and optional
elapsed_sec. Typed views are available from Job and JobSnapshot; raw fields
remain in JobSnapshot.extra["preparation"] for forward compatibility.

Safety semantics: `is_nsfw && !nsfw_detected` means media was withheld. A
completed result with `nsfw_detected=true` was labeled but delivered.

Discovery/metadata: `wait_for_models`, `get_supported_models`,
`get_model_options`, `get_size_presets`, `get_available_models`,
`get_video_asset_config`, `available_loras`, `get_lora`, `supports_loras`,
`lora_constraints`.

Costs: `estimate_cost` (image), `estimate_video_cost`, `estimate_audio_cost`,
`estimate_enhancement_cost`, and low-level forward-compatible `estimate`.

URLs/uploads: v1 `upload_url`, `download_url`, `media_upload_url`,
`media_download_url`; v2 `image_upload_post`, `media_upload_post`, and
`upload_presigned`.

Recovery: `sync(reason)` fetches the app-scoped durable snapshot and replays
media project state. `list_projects_elsewhere` is read-only. The SDK invokes
recovery after socket authentication and after an internal receiver lag.
Terminal failed/canceled recovery settles outstanding waiters and unfinished
jobs, preserving existing errors or the server's reason. Completed jobs remain
unchanged. Local timeouts never imply server cancellation.

## Video frame behavior

Call `calculate_video_frames(model_id, duration, fps, min, max)`.

- WAN 2.2: generation is fixed at 16 FPS; output FPS may represent later
  interpolation. Frames = rounded(duration * 16) + 1.
- LTX families: generate at requested FPS, then snap to `1 + n*8`.
- MiniMax H3: fixed 24 FPS and `124 + n*17`, clamped to supported limits.
- Other video families: rounded(duration * fps) + 1.

Project creation performs local preflight validation for the current MiniMax
H3, Wan 3, Seedance, and HappyHorse asset/task/duration contracts before any
generation request is submitted.
Wan 3 rejects the retired smartDuration field whenever present, including
false or null. Supply an explicit duration from 2 to 30 seconds.

Use runtime model metadata where possible. Model IDs in docs are illustrative.

## ChatApi

Socket-native non-streaming:

```rust
let result = client.chat.create_completion(&serde_json::json!({
  "model": model_id,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "think": false
})).await?;
```

Socket-native streaming returns `ChatStream`, which implements
`futures_util::Stream<Item = Result<ChatChunk>>`. `wait(timeout)` returns the
assembled completion; `final_result()` is available after stream closure.
Tool-call argument fragments are assembled by index.

Supported completion wire options include maxTokens/max_tokens, temperature,
topP/top_p, topK/top_k, minP/min_p, repetition/frequency/presence penalties,
stop, tokenType, billingMode, tools, toolChoice/tool_choice, sogniTools,
sogniToolExecution, taskProfile, responseFormat, safeContentFilter, `think`, and
workload attribution.

`think` maps to `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`. For structured output,
prefer function tools plus required tool choice. Helpers:
`is_sogni_tool_call` and `parse_tool_call_arguments`.

Hosted REST: `create_hosted_completion`. Direct synchronous hosted tools:
`execute_hosted_tool`. The hosted tool manifest has 25 version-pinned entries;
read through `HostedTools` rather than copying schemas.

Durable chat: `create_run`, `get_run`, `cancel_run`, `confirm_run_cost`, and
`stream_run_events`. `Idempotency-Key` and workload attribution are propagated.
SSE resume uses `Last-Event-ID`.

## CreativeWorkflowsApi

`WorkflowStart` accepts exactly one of inline `input` or saved `workflow_id`.
Other fields: `inputs`, `token_type`, `billing_mode`, `app_source`,
`max_estimated_capacity_units`, `confirm_cost`, `media_references`,
`idempotency_key`, and attribution.

Methods: `start`, `list`, `get`, `events`, `stream_events`, `confirm_cost`,
`resume`, `reseed`, `cancel`. Terminal statuses include `completed`, `failed`,
`cancelled`, and `partial_failure`. Waiting reasons are exposed through
`CREATIVE_WORKFLOW_WAITING_REASONS`.

Templates: `workflows.templates.list/get/create/update/delete/fork`.

## Other namespaces

- `ReplayApi`: `write`, `list`, `get`.
- `StatsApi`: `leaderboard`.
- `AnnouncementsApi`: `active`, `dismiss`. Subscribe to `appAlert` at client
  construction when live app alerts are desired.

## Transport, lifecycle, and errors

The shared reqwest client pools HTTP connections, stores cookies, follows a
bounded redirect policy, uses Rustls/native roots, and applies request/connect
timeouts. The WebSocket sends JSON envelopes with a base64-encoded JSON `data`
field, normalizes `jobID`/`imgID` to uppercase, pings periodically, and applies
capped jittered exponential reconnect delay.

SSE APIs return `SseStream`; each `SseEvent` includes event, parsed data, id,
and raw frame. Consumers own endpoint-specific terminal handling and reconnect
policy.

Error variants: `Api`, `Project`, `Chat`, `InvalidInput`, `Protocol`,
`Transport`, `Timeout`, `Closed`, `Json`, `Url`, `Http`, `Io`.
`is_subscription_limit_error` recognizes the stable public subscription error
contract.

Never embed secrets. Credential `Debug` output is redacted. Keep one client
alive, explicitly `close()` it during shutdown, and never interpret a local
timeout as server cancellation.
